Import Item and Ability Parameters from IRT Software

Source: R/bring_output.R
bring.flexmirt.Rd

These functions import item and/or ability parameter estimates from the output files of BILOG-MG 3, PARSCALE 4, and flexMIRT. bring.mirt() imports the item parameters, together with the latent mean and variance, of a model fitted with the mirt R package.

Usage

bring.flexmirt(
  file,
  type = c("par", "sco"),
  rePar = TRUE,
  rePar.gpc = TRUE,
  n.factor = 1
)

bring.bilog(file, type = c("par", "sco"))

bring.parscale(file, type = c("par", "sco"))

bring.mirt(x)

Arguments

file

The path to the output file that contains the item or ability parameter estimates.

type

A character string giving the type of output file: "par" for an item parameter file or "sco" for an ability (score) file. The case is ignored. Default is "par". Not used by bring.mirt().

rePar

Logical. Used only by bring.flexmirt() with type = "par". If TRUE (default), the intercepts of dichotomous and graded response model (GRM) items are converted to difficulty (threshold) parameters and the logits of the guessing parameters to guessing parameters, so that full_df follows the irtQ item metadata format. This requires a unidimensional model. If FALSE, the slope-intercept values in the file are kept, and full_df cannot then be used directly by other irtQ functions.

rePar.gpc

Logical. Used only by bring.flexmirt() with type = "par". If TRUE (default), the nominal model parameters of generalized partial credit model (GPCM) items are converted to a slope and step parameters. The function stops when the file contains a nominal model item or a multidimensional GPCM item; use rePar.gpc = FALSE to read such a file, in which case the scoring function and intercept values are kept and nominal items get the model name "NOMM".

n.factor

An integer giving the number of latent traits (factors). Used only by bring.flexmirt() with type = "sco". Default is 1.

x

A fitted model object returned by mirt::mirt() for a single group and a unidimensional model. The mirt package, listed in Suggests, must be installed to use bring.mirt().

Value

  • bring.flexmirt(): a named list with one element per group (Group1, Group2, ...). With type = "par", each element is a list with id, factor (number of dimensions), cats, model, par (a matrix of item parameters), full_df (the item metadata), mean and cov (the latent mean vector and covariance matrix), and emphist (a data frame with theta and weight, or NULL when no empirical histogram was estimated). With type = "sco", each element is a list with theta and se, plus iter (the number of iterations) or imputation (the imputation number) when the file contains that column. se is NULL for multidimensional models and for imputed values.

  • bring.bilog(): with type = "par", a list with par and full_df; with type = "sco", a list with one element per group code in the file, each a list with theta, se, and full_df (a data frame with group, id, nitem, ncorrect, p, theta, and se).

  • bring.parscale(): with type = "par", a list with id, factor, cats, model, par_parscale (the parameters and standard errors as reported by PARSCALE), par, and full_df; with type = "sco", a data frame with id, theta, and se (a value of 999 becomes NA).

  • bring.mirt(): a list with id, factor, cats, model (a list with the mirt item types, old, and the irtQ model names, new), emphist (a matrix of quadrature points and weights), par_mirt (the mirt parameters), par, full_df, and ability (the latent mean and variance).

Details

The bring.flexmirt() function was developed by modifying the read.flexmirt() function (Pritikin & Falk, 2020). Similarly, bring.bilog() and bring.parscale() were based on modified versions of the read.bilog() and read.parscale() functions (Weeks, 2010), respectively.

The functions read the layout of the file, not its name. The usual files are the ".PAR" and ".SCO" files of BILOG-MG and PARSCALE and the "-prm.txt" and "-sco.txt" files of flexMIRT; other flexMIRT output files (e.g., "-irt.txt") cannot be read. For mirt, the fitted model object is passed directly.

bring.flexmirt() can also read the files of a multidimensional model: item parameter files with rePar = FALSE (and rePar.gpc = FALSE when GPCM items are present), and ability files with n.factor set to the number of factors. The other functions of irtQ work only with unidimensional models.

For polytomous items, bring.flexmirt(), bring.parscale(), and bring.mirt() import the parameters of the graded response model (GRM) and the generalized partial credit model (GPCM); a polytomous mirt item of type "Rasch" is imported as a GPCM item with a slope of 1. bring.bilog() reads dichotomous items only. bring.parscale() does not support the model codes 2, 4, 6, and 8 of PARSCALE for polytomous items and stops with an error when the file has them.

bring.mirt() accepts the item types "Rasch", "2PL", and "3PL" for dichotomous items and "Rasch", "graded", "gpcm", and "gpcmIRT" for polytomous items. A two-category item of a mixed-format test may also be fitted with "graded", "gpcm", or "gpcmIRT". A model fitted to multiple groups is not supported, and the function stops with an error; extract one group first with mirt::extract.group().

In full_df, bring.flexmirt() labels dichotomous items "3PLM" or "2PLM", while bring.bilog(), bring.parscale(), and bring.mirt() label them "DRM", with a guessing parameter of 0 for items without guessing. For bring.mirt(), this includes two-category items fitted with the "graded", "gpcm", or "gpcmIRT" model. Change the model column if another model is wanted in est_irt(), which fits "DRM" items as 3PLM items. The parameters are kept on the scale of the program, and the files do not record the scaling constant; pass the value of D used in the calibration (e.g., 1 for flexMIRT and mirt) to the other irtQ functions.

Note

For an item parameter file, the element full_df of the result is the item metadata (item IDs, numbers of score categories, model names, and item parameters) used by the other functions of irtQ. See info() or simdat() for the metadata format.

For GPCM items, full_df contains the step parameters \(b_v = \beta - \tau_v\), computed from the overall location \(\beta\) and the category parameters \(\tau_v\) reported by the program (PARSCALE) or from the nominal model intercepts (flexMIRT). See the IRT Models section in irtQ-package for the parameterization of the GPCM.

Sample Output Files

Two sample item parameter files are included in the package: the PARSCALE 4 file "parscale_sample.PAR" and the flexMIRT file "flexmirt_sample-prm.txt". Both contain the estimates for the same mixed-format test of 55 items: 50 dichotomous items fit with the 3PL model and five items with five score categories fit with the GRM (items 39, 40, and 53 to 55). The examples below import these files.

References

Cai, L. (2017). flexMIRT 3.5 Flexible multilevel multidimensional item analysis and test scoring (Computer software). Chapel Hill, NC: Vector Psychometric Group.

Chalmers, R. P. (2012). mirt: A multidimensional item response theory package for the R environment. Journal of Statistical Software, 48(6), 1-29. doi:10.18637/jss.v048.i06

Muraki, E., & Bock, R. D. (2003). PARSCALE 4: IRT item analysis and test scoring for rating scale data (Computer software). Chicago, IL: Scientific Software International. URL http://www.ssicentral.com

Pritikin, J. (2018). rpf: Response Probability Functions. R package version 0.59. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=rpf.

Pritikin, J. N., & Falk, C. F. (2020). OpenMx: A modular research environment for item response theory method development. Applied Psychological Measurement, 44(7-8), 561-562. doi:10.1177/0146621620929431 .

Weeks, J. P. (2010). plink: An R Package for Linking Mixed-Format Tests Using IRT-Based Methods. Journal of Statistical Software, 35(12), 1-33. doi:10.18637/jss.v035.i12 .

Zimowski, M. F., Muraki, E., Mislevy, R. J., & Bock, R. D. (2003). BILOG-MG 3: Multiple-group IRT analysis and test maintenance for binary items (Computer software). Chicago, IL: Scientific Software International. URL http://www.ssicentral.com

Examples

## Example 1
# Import the "-prm.txt" output file from flexMIRT
flex_sam <- system.file("extdata", "flexmirt_sample-prm.txt",
                        package = "irtQ")

# Read item parameters and convert them to item metadata
bring.flexmirt(file = flex_sam, "par")$Group1$full_df

## Example 3
# Import the item parameters of a model fitted with the mirt package
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("mirt", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- mirt::mirt(as.data.frame(LSAT6), 1, itemtype = "2PL",
                    verbose = FALSE)
  bring.mirt(fit)$full_df
}
#>            id cats model     par.1      par.2 par.3
#> item.1 item.1    2   DRM 0.8250552 -3.3607460     0

#> item.4 item.4    2   DRM 0.6886588 -1.8657302     0

# }
